tasks.short: Check approved hours, attendance and pay changes before posting them to AFAS.

today.trigger: Daily approved hours or pay changes arrive; the detailed current workflow needs confirmation.
steps: Collect site hours, attendance records and approved pay adjustments.
Match employees, dates and approvals against AFAS records.
Check overtime, shift allowances and adjustments against the applicable CAO.
Ask supervisors to resolve missing approvals or conflicting entries.
Post accepted entries and retain supporting evidence.
systems: Site time records; source system to confirm
drudgery: Checking duplicate entries and missing approvals
today.time_sinks: Repeated checks across three sites and two CAOs, followed by chasing supervisors near payroll cutoff.

lenses.faster: File matching, duplicate checks and preparation of posting lines disappear. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 27 minutes per equivalent batch, including exception review and posting approval.
lenses.autonomous: Receipt of an approved hours batch starts validation and preparation of AFAS entries. The specialist approves the batch after resolving exceptions; unresolved records remain blocked.
lenses.ambitious: New service to site supervisors: a daily payroll readiness report showing missing approvals before cutoff. Demand would grow as its cost falls because supervisors could correct problems during the shift.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying hours or repeatedly checking employee numbers. The specialist gets more time to resolve disputed allowances and explain recurring problems to supervisors.
lenses.options: Compare a corrected current-period entry with an authorised later adjustment, showing employee impact and cutoff consequences. The specialist can choose a lawful correction route with evidence.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from checking every line to investigating exceptions and improving site submission quality. The specialist gains delegated authority to block incomplete batches and propose validation changes, making the work more expert.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's hours-submission completeness checks after learning site approval responsibilities and AFAS import controls.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must resolve conflicting accounts of hours worked, ambiguous CAO treatment and situations where an apparently valid approval hides a real pay problem.
tasks.pattern_why: Employee matching, approval checks, duplicate detection and CAO validation can use explicit rules; a model is unnecessary for routine verification.

in_practice.trigger: An approved site hours file or pay-adjustment batch reaches the controlled intake location.
steps: Validate file structure, employee identifiers, dates and approval evidence.
Apply versioned CAO rules and identify duplicates, overlaps and unusual changes.
Prepare AFAS posting lines and a source-linked exception report.
Present batch totals and unresolved exceptions to the specialist.
After approval, import accepted lines and reconcile imported totals to the source.
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll approves every posting batch; supervisors confirm factual corrections and authorised managers approve pay changes.
systems: AFAS Profit through an integration method to confirm
data_needed: Approved hours and adjustment records
Employee identifiers and employment dates
Effective-dated CAO rules and pay components
Approval matrix and previous posting identifiers
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted payroll audit register with source references, rule versions, approvals and AFAS import results.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 supports automatic approval of Flex declaration payroll lines after a person approves the declaration; this is a narrow precedent for rules after an approval gate.
Explicit rules can validate payroll inputs, but Noordhaven's integrations and CAO mappings require local testing.
The 55% saving is a planning estimate including review, not a measured company or vendor result.

risks: Wrong CAO assignment or effective dates can systematically misstate pay.
Reimported files can duplicate adjustments unless posting identifiers are unique.
Agency worker hours must follow an agency reconciliation route rather than enter Noordhaven employee payroll.
research_questions: Which systems hold approved hours at each site, and do their exports contain stable employee and approval identifiers?
Can AFAS validate and import these components without manual re-entry, with duplicate protection?
What proportion of today's time concerns routine checks versus disputed hours or CAO interpretation?

tasks.short: Run wage and deduction calculations in AFAS and check the results.

today.trigger: Approved payroll inputs are ready for a trial or final calculation.
steps: Confirm employee master data and approved pay inputs are complete.
Check applicable tax, pension, CAO and deduction settings.
Run AFAS payroll calculations.
Review changes in gross pay, deductions and net pay.
Correct authorised errors and rerun affected calculations.
drudgery: Entering the same approved inputs twice
today.time_sinks: Investigating changes between trial runs and correcting input or configuration errors; AFAS already performs the arithmetic.

lenses.faster: Approved-input transfer and routine comparison of calculation results become automatic. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 39 minutes because AFAS already calculates wages and the remaining configuration and exception work needs review.
lenses.autonomous: An approved input snapshot starts an AFAS trial calculation and deterministic validation. Routine calculations run unattended; configuration exceptions stop, and final payroll release remains a separate human decision.
lenses.ambitious: New service to HR Business Partners: checked pay-impact estimates for proposed contract changes before they are offered. Demand would grow if estimates became cheap enough to obtain during employee discussions.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss repeated trial-run comparisons. The specialist gets more time for difficult retroactive adjustments and understandable explanations of deductions.
lenses.options: Use the AFAS calculation engine to compare lawful options such as different start dates or agreed working hours. Showing net-pay and employer-cost differences can change the proposed arrangement.
lenses.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week testing calculation settings and advising on pay consequences. They gain delegated authority to reject unsupported calculation inputs and recommend configuration changes, with greater technical expertise required.
reach: Absorb the Compensation and Benefits Specialist's routine pay-impact modelling after learning pension treatment, benefits taxation and approval boundaries.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must interpret disputed deductions, assess unusual employment arrangements and confirm that a technically correct calculation reflects the employee's actual entitlement.
tasks.pattern_why: Gross-to-net calculations require repeatable statutory and contractual rules in AFAS; generated arithmetic or model-selected deductions are unsuitable.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll inputs receive approval and are frozen for a trial run.
steps: Load approved inputs with effective dates and reconcile their totals.
Run AFAS calculations using the authorised configuration.
Check expected components, deduction continuity and gross-to-net reconciliation.
Route failed checks to the specialist without changing entitlements automatically.
Store the checked results for the separately approved payroll release.
in_practice.human_gate: Humans approve rule and configuration changes, resolve exceptions and authorise final payroll release; routine trial calculations need no individual approval.
systems: Controlled integration or scheduled workflow to confirm
data_needed: Approved wage components and contract terms
Current tax and pension configuration
Applicable CAO and effective dates
Previous payroll results and authorised retroactive changes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS calculation history and a restricted run register recording input versions, checks, exceptions and release approval.

evidence.claim: PayCaptain describes its production payroll calculation as deterministic, rules-based and repeatable, with AI operating around the calculation.
Workday's announced Payroll Agent concerns auditing and notices; its autopilot is described as an early-2027 early-adopter capability, not a current AFAS implementation.
The 35% saving assumes existing AFAS calculation automation and includes retained specialist review.

risks: A wrong pension or CAO configuration can produce plausible but incorrect results for many employees.
Automatically rerunning changed inputs can invalidate an earlier approval unless snapshots are controlled.
Bank payment release must remain subject to Noordhaven's separate financial authorisation controls.
research_questions: How much time remains in data entry and comparison after AFAS's existing payroll functions are used fully?
Can trial calculations be scheduled and results retrieved through supported AFAS functionality?
Which CAO, pension and retroactive-pay cases fail current validation, and who approves configuration changes?

tasks.short: Keep leave balances and absence-related payroll records up to date.

today.trigger: An approved leave request, absence notification or correction reaches HR or payroll.
steps: Retrieve the approved leave or absence event.
Check dates, contracted hours, leave type and applicable entitlement.
Record or verify the event and its effect on balances in AFAS.
Resolve overlaps, negative balances and payroll consequences.
Confirm corrections with the employee or responsible HR colleague.
drudgery: Finding mismatches between leave and hours records
today.time_sinks: Reconciling shift patterns, part-time schedules and corrections received after payroll cutoff.

lenses.faster: Routine balance updates, overlap detection and reconciliation to approved leave events run automatically. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 30 minutes, including review of unusual entitlements and corrections.
lenses.autonomous: An approved AFAS leave event starts balance and payroll-impact checks. Routine updates complete automatically; disputed entitlement, missing schedules and unusual absence-pay changes go to the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: New service to night-shift employees: access to a checked leave balance and the reason for pending corrections outside office hours. Demand would grow because employees could plan leave without waiting for payroll availability.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss recalculating balances after every schedule correction. The specialist gets more time to help employees understand entitlement and resolve difficult cases.
lenses.options: Compare lawful leave-category treatments where the underlying circumstances support more than one route, including their balance and pay effects. The employee and authorised HR colleague choose the appropriate route rather than having software choose it.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward complicated leave entitlements and preventing repeated site errors. The specialist gains authority to settle documented payroll-balance corrections within an agreed mandate and needs deeper Dutch leave-law knowledge.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's leave-balance reconciliation after learning statutory and CAO leave categories; HR Business Partners retain return-to-work case management.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must recognise sensitive personal circumstances, resolve contested entitlement and distinguish payroll administration from medical assessment or return-to-work decisions.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved structured leave events, schedules and entitlement rules support predictable balance updates without model interpretation.

in_practice.trigger: An approved leave or authorised absence event is created or changed in AFAS.
steps: Read event dates, leave category, employment terms and the applicable work schedule.
Apply effective-dated entitlement and balance rules.
Check overlaps, unusual balances and differences from approved hours.
Post routine updates and send unresolved cases to the specialist.
Reconcile balances and payroll effects before the relevant cutoff.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers retain leave approval; payroll reviews disputed entitlement, missing information and unusual absence-pay treatment before any affected change is posted.
data_needed: Approved leave and absence event metadata
Contracted hours and work schedules
Opening balances and previous corrections
Statutory and CAO entitlement rules, excluding medical diagnoses
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS leave history and a restricted payroll correction register with rule versions and approvals.

evidence.claim: Structured leave balances and payroll consequences can be calculated through explicit entitlement rules; Noordhaven's schedule quality determines feasibility.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment of solely automated decisions with significant effects, including applicable safeguards and human intervention rights.
The 50% saving is an estimate for administration and review, not a measured reduction in absence or case-management work.

risks: Incorrect shift schedules can distort leave deductions and balances.
Payroll access must exclude diagnoses and unnecessary occupational-health information under AVG/GDPR.
Wet verbetering poortwachter responsibilities remain with the designated case owners; balance automation must not make return-to-work decisions.
research_questions: Are leave requests, approvals and changing shift schedules recorded reliably in AFAS?
Which leave categories and absence-pay changes account for most manual corrections under the two CAOs?
Can access controls provide the required payroll facts without exposing medical details?

tasks.short: Update payroll records for contract changes, transfers, tax choices and leavers.

today.trigger: An authorised employee change or departure becomes effective.
steps: Receive the approved change and supporting documentation.
Match the employee and check the effective date.
Check consequences for payroll components, tax credit choices and final pay.
Update AFAS payroll fields or verify updates made by HR Administration.
Check the resulting calculation and retain the approval.
systems: SharePoint contract templates and approved documents
drudgery: Re-entering changes already held in HR records
Checking that leaver components have stopped
today.time_sinks: Late changes, conflicting documents and retroactive effects across payroll periods.

lenses.faster: Approved structured changes flow from HR records into payroll with effective-date checks and automatic comparisons. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 27 minutes, including exception handling and checking sensitive changes.
lenses.autonomous: An authorised AFAS HR change starts the payroll update workflow. Supported routine changes post automatically; bank details, disputed departures and unsupported retroactive changes require separate human validation.
lenses.ambitious: New service to transferring employees and their managers: a checked pay-change preview before the transfer takes effect. Demand would grow if it became inexpensive to provide during transfer planning.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing the same change into multiple records. The specialist gets more time to prevent final-pay surprises and support employees through transitions.
lenses.options: Compare permitted transfer dates or correction periods using AFAS calculations and show their consequences. This can change the agreed implementation date before documents are finalised.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward effective-date control and complex final settlements. The specialist gains authority to reject incomplete change requests and approve routine payroll mappings within a documented mandate, increasing the role's expertise.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's payroll-field update checks after learning lifecycle workflows, document authority and segregation of duties.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must interpret conflicting instructions, recognise contentious departures and challenge changes that are formally approved but inconsistent with contractual entitlement.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved structured HR events can map to payroll fields through explicit rules, with exceptions routed instead of inferred.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised, effective-dated HR change is committed in AFAS.
steps: Verify the event's authorisation, employee identity and effective date.
Map supported changes to payroll fields using versioned rules.
Check overlapping events, closed periods and dependent pay components.
Apply routine changes and hold sensitive or unsupported cases.
Compare the next trial calculation with the expected effect and retain the audit trail.
in_practice.human_gate: HR approves the underlying employment change; payroll validates exceptions and final settlements, and bank-detail changes require independent verification.
systems: AFAS workflow or supported integration to confirm
data_needed: Authorised lifecycle events and effective dates
Current payroll fields and component mappings
Documented employee tax-credit choices
Closed-period status and final-settlement rules
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS employee mutation history linked to approvals, mapping versions and calculation checks.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 provides wage-component history, which supports investigation of payroll changes but does not establish the proposed integration.
Effective-dated HR-to-payroll mappings can be deterministic when source approvals and fields are structured.
The 55% saving depends on current duplicate entry and excludes unproven automation of contentious settlements.

risks: A mistaken effective date can affect several payroll periods.
Automatic propagation can spread an incorrect HR record into payroll.
Dutch loonheffingskorting choices must be recorded from valid employee instructions, not inferred from personal circumstances.
research_questions: Which HR changes already update AFAS payroll automatically, and where does duplicate entry remain?
Do authorised events contain reliable effective dates and sufficient approval evidence?
Which change types require independent verification or specialist settlement calculations?

tasks.short: Find payroll discrepancies, trace the cause and get corrections approved.

today.trigger: A trial payroll run, employee query or hours reconciliation reveals a possible discrepancy.
steps: Compare hours, pay components and trial-run results with approved records.
Identify unexpected changes and missing or duplicated components.
Trace each discrepancy to source records and applicable rules.
Agree the correction with the responsible supervisor or HR colleague.
Rerun the calculation and document the resolution.
drudgery: Collecting the same evidence for each exception
today.time_sinks: Tracing causes across hours, contract changes and payroll settings, then chasing a clear factual answer.

lenses.faster: Deterministic checks find candidate discrepancies and a model drafts source-linked explanations. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 24 minutes, including checking the evidence, agreeing corrections and confirming the rerun.
lenses.autonomous: A completed trial run starts fixed checks and an explanation step for flagged items. The specialist decides whether each flag is valid and approves every correction before it affects payroll.
lenses.ambitious: More frequent decision: review new payroll exceptions weekly during peak season instead of discovering them at month close. Demand would grow as review costs fall because earlier decisions leave time to fix agency and site submission problems.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss scanning hundreds of unchanged lines. The specialist gets more time to investigate unusual cases and eliminate recurring causes.
lenses.options: For a confirmed discrepancy, compare supported correction routes, the affected periods and employee cash effects. The choice can change when and how the correction is made, subject to legal and CAO requirements.
lenses.altitude: The week centres on root causes and prevention across sites. The specialist gains delegated authority to stop a run when control checks fail and to require corrective action from input owners, increasing expert judgement.
reach: Absorb the Controller's initial payroll-variance investigation after learning general-ledger mappings, materiality and reconciliation controls.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must distinguish a legitimate unusual payment from an error, assess contradictory evidence and handle corrections fairly when an employee has relied on the original pay.
tasks.pattern_why: A fixed workflow uses deterministic checks to identify exceptions and one model call to explain the retrieved evidence; investigation and correction stay behind a human gate.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS produces a trial-run snapshot with the approved input set.
steps: Run explicit checks for unexpected pay movements, missing pension components, duplicate leaver payments and minimum-wage issues.
Retrieve only the source records needed to explain each flag.
Use one model call per exception to draft a cited explanation, missing facts and a proposed next check.
Have the specialist validate the explanation and authorise any correction.
Rerun deterministic checks and record the approved resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll validates every exception disposition and correction; the model cannot alter wages, dismiss a flag or release payroll.
data_needed: Current and previous payroll snapshots
Approved hours and effective-dated employee changes
Versioned check thresholds and CAO rules
Source references and previous exception outcomes
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted exception register with check results, source references, model version, reviewer decision and correction history.

evidence.claim: PayCaptain documents production checks for unexpected gross-pay changes, stopped pension contributions, duplicate leaver net pay and rates below minimum wage; this is a UK vendor case.
Workday has announced payroll auditing outside defined parameters and drafted employee notices, with autopilot early adoption planned for early 2027.
The 60% estimate includes human exception review; the digest supplies no measured Dutch time saving or error rate.

risks: A convincing generated explanation can misidentify the cause; reviewers must inspect source evidence.
Loose thresholds create alert fatigue, while narrow checks miss unfamiliar errors.
Payroll data sent to a model needs approved access, retention and processing arrangements under AVG/GDPR.
research_questions: Which known past errors would the proposed checks detect, and how many false flags would they create?
Can every generated factual claim be traced to a retrieved source field or document?
Does total investigation time fall after including review, false alarms and correction approval?

tasks.short: Complete arrival and departure records from approved time evidence.

today.trigger: A shift ends or an incomplete time record is submitted.
steps: Collect recorded arrivals, departures and supervisor corrections.
Match records to employees and scheduled shifts.
Identify missing punches, cross-midnight shifts and conflicting entries.
Obtain confirmation for missing or disputed times.
Complete the timesheet and send it for approval.
systems: Site time records; capture method to confirm
AFAS Profit where timesheets are held or imported
drudgery: Copying confirmed times into a standard sheet
today.time_sinks: Missing punches and late supervisor confirmation, especially around night shifts and payroll cutoff.

lenses.faster: Pairing complete time events and formatting timesheets become automatic. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 18 minutes, including checking exceptions and obtaining confirmation; savings depend on reliable captured times.
lenses.autonomous: A completed shift or new time-event file starts pairing and validation. Complete records proceed to normal approval; missing or conflicting times wait for supervisor confirmation and are never filled from the roster alone.
lenses.ambitious: New service to night-shift supervisors: a shift-end queue of missing punches while workers are still available to confirm them. Demand would grow because resolving gaps immediately is easier than reconstructing them at month end.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pairing timestamps or fixing date formats. The specialist gets more time to improve the capture process and resolve disputed records.
lenses.options: Show competing source accounts of a disputed arrival or departure, with their provenance and pay consequences. This helps the supervisor establish the correct record rather than selecting a convenient estimate.
lenses.altitude: The specialist spends less time constructing sheets and more time setting evidence standards for time corrections. They gain authority to reject unsupported records, with greater expertise in shift and working-time treatment.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's consolidation of supervisor-approved timesheets after learning local shift practices and time-record correction procedures.

tasks.human_edge: A person must establish what happened when time evidence is missing or contested; software cannot infer actual attendance from the scheduled shift.
tasks.pattern_why: Pairing structured time events, handling overnight shifts and checking completeness require explicit rules, not a model.

in_practice.trigger: A shift closes or a new structured time-event export arrives.
steps: Validate event identifiers, timestamps, time zones and employee mappings.
Pair arrivals and departures using approved cross-midnight rules.
Flag missing events, duplicates and conflicts without inventing timestamps.
Obtain authorised corrections through the exception workflow.
Produce complete timesheets and retain source-to-output reconciliation.
in_practice.human_gate: Supervisors approve attendance and factual corrections; payroll handles unresolved exceptions, while complete records are assembled automatically.
systems: Existing site time-capture source to confirm
data_needed: Actual time events and stable event identifiers
Employee and agency-worker mappings
Shift schedules for validation only
Approved corrections and time-handling rules
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted time-record audit trail retaining original events, approved corrections and generated timesheet versions.

evidence.claim: Structured timestamp pairing and timesheet generation are deterministic; the company description does not identify a time-capture system or confirm data quality.
Employment-related AI monitoring and evaluation can fall within the AI Act's high-risk categories; the proposed rules-based assembly should not be expanded into employee scoring without assessment.
The 70% saving is conditional on usable electronic time events and may be much lower for paper or frequently incomplete records.

risks: Scheduled hours mistaken for actual attendance can underpay or overpay employees.
Overnight shifts, daylight-saving changes and break rules can create systematic errors.
Changes to employee time monitoring may require OR consent under WOR Article 27; attendance data must not become unapproved individual performance scoring.
research_questions: How are arrivals and departures captured at each site, and what percentage of shifts have complete electronic records?
Who can confirm missing times for night shifts, and how quickly do they respond?
Do cross-midnight, daylight-saving and break cases reconcile correctly against approved historical timesheets?

tasks.short: Prepare new starters' payroll records from approved employment paperwork.

today.trigger: An accepted offer becomes an approved employment contract and the starter's payroll documents arrive.
steps: Collect approved contract details and required payroll information.
Check completeness, identity-verification status and signed employee declarations.
Match documents to the correct starter and resolve inconsistencies.
Enter or verify payroll fields in AFAS.
Check the starter's first trial calculation and outstanding items.
drudgery: Comparing repeated versions of starter documents
today.time_sinks: Incomplete starter packs, late contracts and mismatches between offer details and signed employment terms.

lenses.faster: Document extraction, field comparison and missing-item checklists become automatic. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 27 minutes, including source verification, sensitive-field checks and the first-pay review.
lenses.autonomous: Receipt of an approved starter pack starts extraction into a draft payroll record. Payroll verifies the draft and identity-check status before activation; missing declarations or conflicting terms block completion.
lenses.ambitious: New service to new starters and site managers: a first-pay readiness check before the first shift, with a named owner for each missing item. Demand would grow during seasonal recruitment because it prevents avoidable first-pay problems.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying addresses and contract hours. The specialist gets more time to help starters with unfamiliar Dutch payroll forms and prevent errors that damage early trust.
lenses.options: Where payroll cutoff is at risk, compare an authorised regular-run route with an available off-cycle route and show timing and operational consequences. This changes the action taken to secure correct first pay.
lenses.altitude: The specialist becomes responsible for first-pay readiness rather than starter-data transcription. They gain authority to block payroll activation when required evidence is missing and need stronger document and identity-control expertise.
reach: Absorb the HR Administrator's payroll starter-pack completeness checks after learning onboarding ownership, identity-verification procedures and secure document handling.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must verify conflicting contractual terms, recognise suspicious documentation and support a starter who cannot complete a standard digital process.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call extracts messy contract and form content into a checkable schema; fixed validation and human approval govern payroll activation.

in_practice.trigger: An approved employment contract and starter documents enter the restricted onboarding workflow.
steps: Confirm the pack belongs to a direct employee and retrieve only necessary payroll documents.
Extract permitted fields into a draft schema with source locations and missing-value flags.
Apply deterministic completeness, effective-date and cross-document checks.
Have payroll verify the draft and independently validate sensitive details.
Create the approved AFAS record and check the first trial calculation.
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll approves every new payroll record; authorised staff perform identity verification and independent bank-detail checks outside model judgement.
data_needed: Signed contract and approved employment terms
Required payroll declarations and verified starter details
Identity-verification status from authorised staff
AFAS field schema and applicable CAO mapping
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted onboarding audit register and AFAS creation history, with document references, extracted-field provenance and approval.

evidence.claim: Models can extract document fields into a fixed schema for human checking; the digest provides no documented AFAS starter-intake implementation.
The WOR establishes consent rights for relevant employee-data arrangements; OR involvement must be assessed before introducing new personnel-document processing.
The 55% saving is an unvalidated estimate including document verification and first-pay checking.

risks: Extraction errors in salary, hours or dates can appear plausible; original evidence must remain visible.
BSNs, identity documents and bank details require strict access and processing limits under AVG/GDPR; exclude them from model processing where unnecessary.
Agency workers must enter the appropriate agency administration route rather than become Noordhaven payroll employees.
research_questions: Which starter fields are already transferred from Recruitee or AFAS onboarding, and which still require manual entry?
Can extraction achieve acceptable field accuracy on actual Dutch contracts, scans and signed declarations after review time is included?
Can the approved processing environment minimise sensitive data while preserving a complete source and approval trail?

tasks.short: Combine approved hours, production inputs and payroll data into a reconciled payroll dataset.

today.trigger: A payroll preparation cycle or agreed reporting deadline starts.
steps: Collect hours, approved production-related pay inputs and AFAS payroll extracts.
Standardise employee identifiers, dates, pay codes and site labels.
Combine records and separate direct employees from agency workers.
Check totals, missing records and duplicate entries.
Deliver the reconciled dataset and explain unresolved differences.
systems: Site time and production records; sources to confirm
today.time_sinks: Inconsistent identifiers and file formats, missing submissions and explaining differences between live records and the nightly AFAS extract.

lenses.faster: Scheduled extraction, standardisation, joins and control totals replace recurring spreadsheet preparation. Estimated specialist time falls from 60 to 15 minutes, including review of incomplete feeds and reconciliation exceptions.
lenses.autonomous: Arrival of the expected source files starts a scheduled compilation. Reconciled datasets publish automatically to authorised users; missing sources, broken mappings or failed totals stop publication and alert payroll.
lenses.ambitious: New service to the Controller and site managers: a weekly view of approved labour-cost inputs, including agency hours awaiting invoices. Demand would grow because it supports staffing decisions before month close.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding spreadsheet joins or fixing date formats. The specialist gets more time to explain labour-cost movements and improve source-data quality.
lenses.options: Compare an actuals-only view with an explicitly labelled view including approved but unbilled agency hours. This can change whether Finance treats a movement as a real staffing change or a timing difference.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving data-quality failures and explaining labour-cost coverage. The specialist gains delegated authority to withhold incomplete payroll datasets and approve payroll mapping changes with the HRIS owner, increasing data expertise.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's recurring payroll extract preparation after learning supported AFAS extraction, data modelling and access controls.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist must decide whether apparently comparable records represent the same pay obligation and explain business changes that a clean data join cannot establish.
tasks.pattern_why: Recurring extraction, mapping, joins and reconciliations are predictable data-processing steps; a model adds no necessary capability.

in_practice.trigger: The scheduled collection window opens and expected source exports arrive.
steps: Retrieve authorised exports and record their timestamps and coverage.
Validate schemas and map identifiers, pay codes and site labels.
Combine approved records while keeping employee payroll and agency obligations distinct.
Reconcile source totals, duplicates, missing records and prior-period changes.
Publish the versioned dataset only when controls pass; route failures to payroll.
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll resolves failed controls and approves new mappings; routine reconciled datasets publish within an already approved access and reporting scope.
systems: AFAS supported exports or connectors to confirm
data_needed: Approved hours and any authorised production-related pay inputs
AFAS employee, pay-component and payroll extracts
Agency identifiers, approved hours and relevant invoice references
Versioned mappings, source control totals and refresh timestamps
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted data-pipeline run register recording source coverage, mapping versions, reconciliations, failures and published dataset versions.

evidence.claim: Recurring payroll extraction, joins and control-total reconciliation can run through deterministic data pipelines; source access at Noordhaven remains unconfirmed.
AFAS extracts and nightly Power BI refreshes are part of the supplied company scenario, not proof of live payroll-cutoff integration.
The 75% saving is a workflow estimate including failed-feed review, not a documented customer result.

risks: A technically successful join can duplicate hours or drop workers with unmatched identifiers.
Nightly Power BI data may be stale for a live payroll cutoff; source timestamps must remain visible.
Production information must be limited to authorised pay inputs and must not become unapproved worker performance scoring.
Agency costs and employee wages can be double-counted if their populations and accounting treatment are mixed.
research_questions: Can each source provide stable identifiers, agreed control totals and a supported export at the required time?
Are production measures actually used in authorised pay calculations, and which records belong in this dataset?
Can the pipeline reproduce an approved historical period exactly, including agency separation and late corrections?
Which compilation steps overlap with hours verification and discrepancy review, so savings are not counted twice?

role.altitude: The Payroll Specialist becomes the operational lead for payroll reliability and first-pay readiness. Their week centres on complex exceptions, CAO interpretation, configuration testing and coaching site input owners, with delegated authority to reject unsupported inputs and stop failed runs; final release and employment decisions retain their existing approval owners.
reach: HR Administrator: payroll starter-pack completeness, lifecycle update checks and leave reconciliation, requiring onboarding and entitlement knowledge.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: recurring payroll extract preparation and mapping maintenance, requiring data-modelling and integration skills.
Controller: initial payroll-variance investigation and supporting reconciliation, requiring general-ledger and financial-control knowledge.
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: routine AFAS-based pay-impact estimates, requiring benefits, pension and tax knowledge.
role.ceiling_note: These eight tasks represent 778.1 annual hours, about 49% of the supplied 1,600-hour role baseline. Existing AFAS automation, overlapping task boundaries, payroll peaks and one-person cover constrain recoverable capacity; validate distinct task timings before adding savings or assigning adjacent work, and maintain trained backup and independent approvals.
skills_to_grow: Effective-dated configuration and testing for both CAOs, Dutch tax and pension rules
AFAS workflow, supported integrations and payroll audit controls
Data reconciliation, identifier mapping and controlled automation
Checking generated explanations against source evidence
AVG/GDPR data minimisation and assessment of applicable OR consent rights
Explaining pay decisions and resolving disputed employee cases
Recognising when an AI use crosses into employee monitoring, evaluation or other regulated decision support
role.ambitious_version: Provide dependable first-pay and pay-change readiness services across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, including access for night shifts, while giving Finance timely reconciled labour-cost inputs. Track first-time-right pay, corrections per run and first-pay readiness alongside week-one onboarding, 90-day retention and manager satisfaction; test the contribution to those outcomes rather than assuming payroll automation causes them.
